data.title: Storms batter Europe hitting power supplies, flights and phones
data.description: LONDON - Storms battered northern Europe Sunday cutting power to more than 150,000 homes, disrupting travel and phone networks.

data.title: Nigeria widens hunt for possible Ebola cases
data.description: ABUJA - Nigeria has widened a hunt for potential Ebola cases, with an additional nine contacts traced, health authorities said Sunday.

data.title: Shock and grief in a Jordanian village after church attack
data.description: HAMMOUD (JORDAN) - Workers were cleaning the last traces of blood from St George's Church in Jordan's Hammoud the day after a deadly attack, when visitors arrived to express their solidarity amid an atmosphere of shock and grief.

data.title: Ukraine war divides Bulgaria as voters elect president
data.description: SOFIA (BULGARIA) - Bulgarians were voting in a presidential election on Sunday, as security concerns swirl following a series of drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea.

data.title: UK PM calls for 'honest discussion' about EU free movement
data.description: LONDON - UK leader Andy Burnham indicated he was open to readopting the European Union's free movement rules as part of Britain's future relationship with the bloc, said a report published Sunday.

data.title: Far-right leader Le Pen kicks off tilt at French presidency amid nationwide protests
data.description: ORLéANS (FRANCE) - Marine Le Pen, France's far-right candidate to succeed President Emmanuel Macron in elections in six months, was to give her first campaign speech on Sunday, a day after protests sweeping the country again flared into violence.

data.title: Police made 1,314 arrests in France's protests: government
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Police arrested 1,314 people in weekend protests across France, the interior ministry said Sunday, adding that 53 officers were hurt in clashes.

data.title: Demonstrators wounded as Portugal police clear housing protest camps
data.description: MADRID - Portuguese police again cleared tents set up by protesters against skyrocketing housing prices overnight Sunday, with organisers criticising the brutality of the officers involved.

data.title: Serbia votes with ruling party facing ascendant student movement
data.description: BELGRADE - Polls opened in Serbia on Sunday in what is set to be its most fiercely contested parliamentary election in more than 14 years, as a student-led movement seeks to oust the party of veteran leader Aleksandar Vucic.

data.title: Laos and Cambodia join forces to boost tourism
data.description: Laos and Cambodia are stepping up tourism cooperation under the slogan “Two Countries, One Destination”, with plans to improve cross-border travel and promote joint tourism routes showcasing their natural attractions and cultural heritage.

data.title: Sri Lankan turbine project fuels anger as fish hauls plunge
data.description: MANNAR (SRI LANKA) - Beneath rotating wind turbines on Sri Lanka's Mannar peninsula, a fishing net is hauled up the beach by tractor winches and 20 men, but once again the catch is meagre.

data.title: Mona Lisa off limits as Paris shuts museums over protest fears
data.description: PARIS - Disappointed tourists ‌poked their heads through the Louvre's locked gates on Saturday, shut off from the Mona Lisa as galleries and museums across Paris closed as a precaution ahead of fresh demonstrations.

data.title: Riyadh airport resumes flights following Houthi attacks
data.description: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia - Riyadh's international airport said flights would resume on Sunday after a two-week closure following strikes from Yemen's Houthis on the Saudi capital, though the Iran-backed group warned of more to come.

data.title: More Lula, or back to the Bolsonaros? Brazil votes in cliffhanger
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO, Brazil - Brazilians head to the polls on Sunday facing a stark choice: another four years under veteran leftist Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, or a return to the right under Senator Flavio Bolsonaro.

data.title: Yemen's Houthis renew warning against using Riyadh airport
data.description: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis ​on Sunday renewed their ‌warning against using Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, hours after the airport announced it will designate two terminals for flights following a suspension earlier ​this ⁠month.

data.title: Obama blasts Trump's 'chaos and cruelty' while campaigning for Democrats
data.description: WASHINGTON - Former US president Barack Obama delivered scathing criticisms of his successor, Donald Trump, at rallies on Saturday in Ohio and Michigan to support Democratic candidates ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections.

data.title: Thousands protest in Turkey over journalists' arrests, media shutdowns
data.description: ISTANBUL - Thousands rallied in Istanbul and Ankara on Saturday against what they described as growing pressure on journalists in Turkey, including arrests, media shutdowns and the appointment of state administrators.

data.title: Thousands gather at new Albanian anti-government rally
data.description: TIRANA (ALBANIA) - Thousands rallied in Tirana on Saturday at a fresh anti-government rally after days of violent unrest in the Albanian capital, with police firing tear gas to disperse the crowd.

data.title: French police fire tear gas during fresh protests
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - French police fired tear gas on Saturday to prevent protesters in several cities from advancing to their centres, in fresh nationwide demonstrations held a week after riots broke out, AFP journalists saw.

data.title: Nigeria's Tinubu defends record as economy bites ahead of election
data.description: KADUNA (NIGERIA) - President Bola Tinubu kicked off his re-election campaign Saturday promising "a better tomorrow" as Nigeria prepares to head to the polls in a vote set to be defined by the rising cost of living.

data.title: Israeli forces displace Hebron families after deadly attack
data.description: HEBRON (PALESTINIAN TERRITORIES) - Israeli forces pushed into the occupied West Bank city of Hebron on Saturday and displaced around 250 families, vowing to exact a heavy price for an attack the day before in which two Palestinians killed two soldiers before being gunned down.

data.title: France extends detention of suspected racist shooter
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Police found a copy of Adolf Hitler's "Mein Kampf" at the home of the man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs that killed one person and wounded five, a source close to the investigation told AFP Saturday.

data.title: Seen and heard at protests in France
data.description: PARIS - AFP has deployed reporters, photographers and video journalists in cities across France to document massive cost-of-living protests expected to take place nationwide on Saturday.

data.title: North Korean leader makes unannounced visit to Chinese border city
data.description: SEOUL - North Korean leader Kim Jong Un appears to have arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong, a government source in Seoul and South Korean media said on Saturday.

data.title: Thai foreign minister welcomes US-Myanmar engagement
data.description: LISBON - Thailand welcomes ​US engagement with Myanmar and expects discussions at the Asean summit next month in Manila on how to ‌proceed with the member barred since the 2021 coup, Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said on Friday.

data.title: Security high as France braces for new protests
data.description: PARIS - France was erecting a ring of steel in major cities ahead of new protests Saturday, with police, helicopters and armoured vehicles seeking to prevent a repeat of the violence and looting which erupted during nationwide demonstrations last weekend.
